Quantifier coverage checked: (b)'s identities (I1)/(I2) are exact over Q in the 2m^2=32 real entries of U, so with W1's unitarity substitution they cover every U in U(4), and W2 covers every unambiguous assignment E; the two universal quantifiers in the statement are carried by (b) plus written steps. Residual defect: the sole cited semantic anchor for A_B(n) = <n|out_B> is 'cross-validated against both float engines by tests/test_p3_poly_k1.py' — a k=1-named test — while this claim has k=0, m=4; no m=4-specific cross-validation of bell_amp_poly is cited anywhere in the record, so the physical meaning of the permanent polynomials at this claim's own parameter point rests on an indirect anchor (the identity checks themselves are syntactic). [k0_m4_p_avg_bound.json machine_checked (b): 'cross-validated against both float engines by tests/test_p3_poly_k1.py' vs top-level fields "k":0, "m":4]

Identity-count mismatch between two fields of the same record: machine_checked (b) declares 'two polynomial identities' for every output mode i (4 modes) and Bell pair (B, B'), which yields 128 (ordered pairs) or 80 (unordered incl. diagonal), while the 02:40:15 pack detail reports '64 identities; bound 1/2'. 64 fits 4x16 only if the (I1),(I2) pair is counted as one identity; neither field states the counting convention, leaving the disclosed verification boundary ambiguous on how many checks were replayed. Otherwise statement/evidence/notes agree: the file's claim_statement is character-identical to the ledger statement, the embedded lemma_certificate statement is identical to the dependency text, and its objective field (coefficients -1 on sA, sB, -4 on c, +1 on each lam_*) encodes exactly 'sum_B lambda_B <= s_A + s_B + 4c'. [Evidence entry @ 2026-10-27T02:40:15+00:00 detail '64 identities' vs machine_checked (b) 'two polynomial identities' per mode and Bell pair]

The only machine-checked inequality is (c), an arithmetic comparison 'claimed_p_avg_bound >= (0 + 1)/(0 + 2)'; all operator-order content lives in written_steps outside machine replay. I rechecked each step: W2 (unambiguity per the statement's parenthetical forces G(n) rank-one on e_B, so D_i - Lambda_i = sum over unassigned n of n_i G(n) is PSD), W3 (D_i is the transpose of the Bell-basis matrix of Ohat_i; transposition preserves PSD, Lambda_i real diagonal), W4 (O_A(i) = conj(u)u^T is rank<=1 PSD with trace |U_i0|^2+|U_i1|^2, c_i=0 at k=0, matching the lemma's unit-vector hypotheses), W5 (every pattern has 2 photons so sum_i tr Lambda_i = 2 sum_B p_B), W6 (unit columns give sums 2+2+0, hence (1/4) sum_B p_B <= 1/2). No gap found between (b)'s identities, the lemma gated by (a), and the stated bound; the disclosure in written_steps meets the charter's CERTIFIED boundary, so the level does not overclaim — but the machine-checked share of the inequality chain is thin relative to the written share, and the receipt carries that weight. [k0_m4_p_avg_bound.json written_steps W1–W6 and machine_checked (a)–(c), checked against the charter CERTIFIED definition (Empiricist v1, section 3)]

The statement text fixes the mode-to-qubit assignment ('qubit A on modes 1-2, qubit B on modes 3-4') but not the Fock encoding of the four Bell states nor the definition of p_B; both are supplied only by the evidence setting field ('mode 1 (qubit A) and mode 3 (qubit B) carrying |0>', 'p_B = sum over patterns mapped to B of Pr[pattern | B]'). The receipt binds to the statement text, which leaves these conventions implicit (the bound itself is invariant under rail relabeling, so no loss of truth, only of self-containment). Likewise, restricting the assignment domain to 'two-photon detection patterns' tacitly uses photon-number conservation of a passive U (all other patterns have probability zero), made explicit only in W5 and the setting field. [Statement phrases 'dual-rail Bell pair (qubit A on modes 1-2, qubit B on modes 3-4)' and 'two-photon detection patterns' vs k0_m4_p_avg_bound.json setting field and written_steps W5]

Gate ordering and coverage verified: the certification stamp (2026-10-27T02:39:17) precedes the certified-hash replay (02:40:15, binary_hash matching 53eacdb...); the golden suite exercises this claim's exact parameter point and its failure modes (moment-k0-m4-half expects PASS, moment-k0-m4-corrupt-lemma expects FAIL, plus foreign-lemma and bound-too-low FAIL cases), so the PASS is discriminating; the sole dependency P3.one_body_usd_lemma is CERTIFIED and standing CURRENT, satisfying the level cap, and is actively gated by machine check (a).
